defect: `uucore::fsxattr::has_acl` switched unconditionally from `xattr::list` (non-dereferencing `llistxattr`) to `xattr::list_deref` (dereferencing `listxattr`), while `ls.rs` calls `has_acl(item.path())` even when `item.must_dereference` is `false` (`ls -ld symlink`), causing `ls -ld` on a symlink pointing to an ACL-bearing target to wrongly display a `+` ACL marker on the symlink itself.
trigger: Create a symlink to a directory/file that has a POSIX ACL and run `ls -ld <symlink>` (without `-L`).
match_rule: Connect `has_acl` unconditionally calling `xattr::list_deref` in `fsxattr.rs` to `ls.rs` calling `has_acl` for symlinks when `!item.must_dereference`.
near_misses: Noting only that `xattr::list_deref` follows symlinks without connecting it to `ls`'s non-dereferencing `ls -l`/`ls -ld` path.
why_findable: Checking the callers of `has_acl` in `src/uu/ls/src/ls.rs` immediately shows `ls` calls `has_acl` unconditionally for every long-format item regardless of `item.must_dereference`.
notes: `c674cf18` is a 1-parent squash commit (48 lines). Verified against `c674cf18^` which used `xattr::list` (no deref).

defect: Adding `--algorithm=sha2` made `create_sha2` emit tag names `"SHA224"`/`"SHA256"`/`"SHA384"`/`"SHA512"` and updated `process_non_algo_based_line` for `sha2`, while `identify_algo_name_and_length` still requires exact equality `algo_name_input == Some(&algorithm)` (rejecting `"sha2"` vs `"sha256"`) and only allows explicit bit-lengths for `BLAKE2B` and `SHA3` (omitting `SHA2`), so `cksum -a sha2 --check` rejects both `SHA256 (f) = ...` and `SHA2-256 (f) = ...` lines.
location: src/uucore/src/lib/features/checksum.rs:284-308 (`create_sha2`) and src/uucore/src/lib/features/checksum.rs:854-868 (`identify_algo_name_and_length` bitlen match) vs src/uucore/src/lib/features/checksum.rs:834-853 (`identify_algo_name_and_length` `algo_name_input` check, outside hunk)
trigger: Run `cksum -a sha2 -l 256 f | cksum -a sha2 --check` (or verify a `SHA2-256 (f) = ...` line with `cksum -a sha2 -c`).
match_rule: Relate `create_sha2` emitting `SHA224`/`SHA256`/`SHA384`/`SHA512` (and `cksum -a sha2` passing `algo_name_input = Some("sha2")`) to `identify_algo_name_and_length` rejecting `algo_name_input != Some(&algorithm)` and omitting `ALGORITHM_OPTIONS_SHA2` in the bitlen match.
near_misses: Flagging only the `TODO: hashsum specific` comment without noticing the `sha2` tagged-checksum verification mismatch in `identify_algo_name_and_length`.
why_findable: Comparing `create_sha2` (which tags digests as `SHA256`, etc.) and `process_non_algo_based_line` (which handles `ALGORITHM_OPTIONS_SHA2 | ALGORITHM_OPTIONS_SHA3`) against `identify_algo_name_and_length` immediately exposes both missing `sha2` cases.
notes: Verified against `dfda5e0d^`, where `--algorithm=sha2` did not exist. The `TODO` in `dfda5e0d` is unrelated (`hashsum` removal).

defect: In `open_or_create_subdir`, after `stat_at` returns `NotFound`, `parent_fd.mkdir_at(name, mode)?` propagates `AlreadyExists` as a fatal error instead of retrying/opening the directory when a concurrent `install -D` creates the same directory in the window between `stat_at` and `mkdir_at`.
trigger: Run two `install -D` processes concurrently targeting files in the same not-yet-existing directory tree.
match_rule: Identify the `stat_at -> NotFound -> mkdir_at?` race in `open_or_create_subdir` failing with `AlreadyExists` when a concurrent process creates the directory between `stat_at` and `mkdir_at`.
near_misses: Flagging only symlink replacement semantics (separate issue `[210]`) without noticing the `NotFound -> mkdir_at` `EEXIST` race under parallel `install -D`.
why_findable: Directly visible in `open_or_create_subdir` in `0c412999`: `stat_at` returning `NotFound` followed by unguarded `mkdir_at?` fails whenever another process creates `name` first (whereas previous `fs::create_dir_all` handled `AlreadyExists`).
notes: Local control (`relation: false`). Verified against `0c412999^` which used `std::fs::create_dir_all` (which handles concurrent `AlreadyExists`).

defect: `parse_tabstops` allows `0` for `/N` and `+N` specifiers (`parse_tab_num(..., true)`) and stores `Some(0)` in `TabConfig.increment_size`/`extend_size`, while `next_tabstop` checks `.is_none()` (treating `Some(0)` as an active increment/extension and dividing/modulo by `0` or miscomputing tab positions) instead of treating `Some(0)` as disabled (`None`), breaking `unexpand -t 3,/0` and `unexpand -t 3,+0`.
location: src/uu/unexpand/src/unexpand.rs:50-125 (`parse_tabstops` storing `Some(0)`) vs src/uu/unexpand/src/unexpand.rs:298-335 (`next_tabstop` checking `.is_none()`, outside hunk)
trigger: Run `unexpand -t 3,/0` or `unexpand -t 3,+0` on input containing spaces beyond column 3.
match_rule: Connect `parse_tabstops` storing `Some(0)` into `increment_size`/`extend_size` to `next_tabstop` branching on `Some(n)` / `.is_none()` and dividing by `0` (or failing to treat `0` as no repeating tabstops).
near_misses: Flagging only comma/space separator parsing in `parse_tabstops` without connecting `Some(0)` to `next_tabstop`'s zero-divisor / `.is_none()` handling.
why_findable: Relates `parse_tabstops` explicitly allowing `0` (`allow_zero = true`) for `/0` and `+0` to `next_tabstop` matching `Some(inc)` and computing `% inc` / `increment_size.is_none()`.
notes: Verified against `fa24992b^`, which did not support `/N` or `+N` extended tabstop syntax.

defect: Inside the directory-entry loop of `safe_remove_dir_recursive_impl`, `error = handle_error_with_force(...)` (and `error = handle_unlink(...)` / `handle_permission_denied(...)`) overwrites `error` instead of OR-ing (`error |= ...`), clearing a previously recorded `error = true` if a later entry succeeds or returns `false`. Returning `false` from `safe_remove_dir_recursive_impl` makes the caller believe the directory is empty and attempt to unlink the parent directory, emitting a spurious second "Directory not empty" error.
trigger: Run `rm -rf` on a directory containing an unremovable entry (e.g., inside a non-writable directory) alongside another entry whose handling returns `false` on Linux, clearing `error` so `rm` attempts to remove the non-empty parent and emits a spurious "Directory not empty" error.
match_rule: Identify `error = handle_error_with_force(...)` overwriting the accumulated `error` boolean instead of `error |= handle_error_with_force(...)` in `safe_remove_dir_recursive_impl`.
near_misses: Flagging only `handle_error_with_force` return value without identifying the `=` vs `|=` assignment overwriting prior errors in the loop.
why_findable: Directly visible inside the loop in `safe_remove_dir_recursive_impl` introduced in `45e6cbd1`: sibling branches use `error |= ...` while lines 247 and 278 use plain `error = ...`.

defect: When `libc::mkfifo` returns `-1` (for example, `EEXIST` because the target path already exists), `uumain` prints the error with `show!(...)` without `continue;`, falling straight through to `fs::set_permissions(&f, fs::Permissions::from_mode(mode as u32))` and silently overwriting the permissions of the existing file or FIFO.
trigger: Run `mkfifo -m 0600 existing_file` where `existing_file` already exists with different permissions.
match_rule: Identify the missing `continue` after `if err == -1 { show!(...); }` in `mkfifo::uumain`, causing `fs::set_permissions` to chmod an existing file after `mkfifo` fails.
near_misses: Flagging only the `0o666` umask calculation without spotting the missing `continue` before `fs::set_permissions`.
why_findable: Directly visible in the 12-line hunk in `31ffc3a0`: `if err == -1 { show!(...); }` is immediately followed by unconditional `fs::set_permissions(&f, ...)` inside the `for f in fifos` loop.
notes: Local control (`relation: false`). Verified against `31ffc3a0^`, which passed `mode` directly to `mkfifo()` and never called `fs::set_permissions`.

defect: `PREFERRED_TZ_MAPPINGS` maps fixed-offset abbreviations (`EST`/`EDT`, `PST`/`PDT`, `CST`/`CDT`, `MST`/`MDT`) to DST-observing IANA zones (`America/New_York`, etc.), and `resolve_tz_abbreviation` resolves the zone's offset at the input timestamp (`ts.to_zoned(tz).offset()`), applying the date's seasonal DST offset rather than the fixed UTC offset denoted by the abbreviation (e.g., `2026-01-15 10:00 EDT` uses UTC-5 instead of UTC-4).
match_rule: Identify `PREFERRED_TZ_MAPPINGS` mapping both standard and daylight abbreviations (`EST`/`EDT`, `PST`/`PDT`, etc.) to the same DST-aware IANA zone so `ts.to_zoned(tz).offset()` ignores whether the abbreviation specifies standard or daylight offset.
near_misses: Flagging only ambiguous abbreviation disambiguation (e.g., US vs Australia `EST`) without catching that `EDT` vs `EST` collapse to the same DST-switching IANA zone.
why_findable: Directly visible in the single hunk of `49c3386d`: `("EST", "America/New_York")` and `("EDT", "America/New_York")` map to the identical zone string, which `resolve_tz_abbreviation` immediately queries with `ts.to_zoned(tz)`.
notes: Local control (`relation: false`). Both table and resolver live in one contiguous hunk in `49c3386d`.

defect: When `--userspec=USER` (without `:GROUP`) is given, the `UserOnly` arm computes `let gid = uid as libc::gid_t;` instead of using the user's primary GID from passwd, setting the chrooted process's group ID to its numeric user ID whenever `uid != gid`.
trigger: Run `chroot --userspec=<user> / <cmd>` for a user whose numeric UID differs from their primary GID (e.g., `sync`).
match_rule: Identify `let gid = uid as libc::gid_t;` in the `UserOnly` branch assigning the user's UID to `gid` instead of looking up the user's primary GID.
near_misses: Flagging supplemental `--groups` parsing without spotting `let gid = uid as libc::gid_t;` in `UserOnly`.
why_findable: Directly visible in `b29d8f10`: `let gid = uid as libc::gid_t;` casts `uid` directly into `gid`.

defect: Moving `File::create(s)` for `-o` out of `shuf_exec` to the top of `uumain` creates and truncates the output file BEFORE `read_input_file(&filename)?` opens and reads the input file, truncating an existing `-o` file when input fails to open and wiping all contents on in-place `shuf -o file file`.
trigger: Run `shuf -o out nonexistent_input` (truncates `out`) or `shuf -o file file` (truncates `file` before reading it).
match_rule: Identify `File::create(s)` moved above `read_input_file(&filename)?` in `uumain`, truncating `-o` before reading input.
near_misses: Flagging only `-n 0` touching the output file without noticing `File::create(s)` now executes before `read_input_file(&filename)?`.
why_findable: Directly visible in the `uumain` hunk of `cdd1052c`: `File::create(s)` is hoisted to line 106 above `read_input_file(&filename)?` at line 135 (previously `File::create` ran inside `shuf_exec` after `read_input_file`).

defect: `OdOptions::new` removed the `if st.len() == 1` check and calls `*(st.first().expect("should be caught by clap")) as char`, relying on clap to reject empty strings, but `uu_app` (outside the diff) defines `Arg::new(options::ADDRESS_RADIX)` without `NonEmptyStringValueParser`, so `od -A ''` passes `Some("")` into `OdOptions::new` and panics in both debug and release builds.
location: src/uu/od/src/od.rs:178-181 (`OdOptions::new` `st.first().expect("should be caught by clap")`) vs src/uu/od/src/od.rs:263-270 (`uu_app` `options::ADDRESS_RADIX`, outside diff)
match_rule: Connect `st.first().expect("should be caught by clap")` in `OdOptions::new` to `uu_app` defining `options::ADDRESS_RADIX` without a non-empty value parser, causing a panic on `od -A ''`.
near_misses: Flagging only trailing-character handling like `-Anone` without checking `uu_app`'s `ADDRESS_RADIX` definition to verify whether clap rejects empty strings.
why_findable: The diff explicitly asserts `expect("should be caught by clap")`; checking `Arg::new(options::ADDRESS_RADIX)` in `uu_app` (outside the diff) immediately shows clap accepts empty string values.
notes: Verified against `5ca995b2^`, where `if st.len() == 1 { ... } else { return Err(...) }` cleanly returned an error for empty `-A ''`. Panics in release builds.

near_misses: Flagging only `dired.rs` `//DIRED//` offset output or `DiredAndZeroAreIncompatible` without tracing the earlier `format == Format::Long` guard on `parse_time_style`.
